claims.statement: EMA states that CTIS supports sponsors and authorities through the trial lifecycle and records formal milestones such as the start and end of recruitment, but CTIS is not described as a site-payment ledger.
A 2025 industry meeting summary reports persistent site-payment problems and demand for detailed, real-time reconciliation portals and remittance information.

A 2025 Society for Clinical Research Sites resource says sites want participant payments at the visit with later data entry reconciled seamlessly, demonstrating an adjacent event-to-payment workflow need.

contrary_evidence: Investigator and participant payment products already exist, so a narrow smaller-sponsor wedge and interoperability advantage must be demonstrated.
CTIS lifecycle milestones do not by themselves prove that operational visit data can or should trigger payments.

economics.acquisition_route: One boutique CRO or specialist site-network design partner, followed by clinical finance consultants and EDC integrators
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 5-7 year route would require dozens of concurrent studies, several million annual billable events, repeat CRO channels, and high retained software revenue; enterprise validation cycles make timing uncertain
economics.founder_time: Approximately 12-18 hours per week, with clinical quality, privacy, and payment compliance owned by experienced contractors and partners
economics.gross_margin_basis: Rules software and data integration less validation, security, payment-provider, and clinical finance support costs
economics.payback: Sponsor payback could come from fewer finance exceptions and stronger site relationships; quantified delay and reconciliation costs must be proven on a study ledger
economics.pricing: Approximately 20,000-50,000 PLN per study setup plus 8-25 PLN per accepted visit or other billable event and optional payment-file fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each active trial generates recurring events for years and successful sponsors or CROs launch further studies

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A library of protocol-to-budget mappings and exception outcomes could shorten study setup and predict underpayment or accrual errors
fingerprint.customer: Small and mid-sized EU biotech sponsors, specialist CROs, and multi-site clinical research networks
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner with boutique CROs, clinical finance consultants, and Polish or Central European specialist site networks
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Budget digitisation, milestone adapters, exception approval, payment-provider file generation, and site-facing remittance detail
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The sponsor pays an implementation fee and usage fees when an accepted clinical event becomes an approved site-payment instruction and receipt
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A participant visit or non-visit milestone is accepted but site earnings, invoices, payment schedules, and remittance advice do not reconcile cleanly

founder_fit: The founder's health, neuroscience, and data background supports clinical workflow comprehension
Rule mapping and anomaly detection can use AI without making clinical decisions
A boutique-CRO channel is compatible with a focused technical founder rather than an influencer model
risks: Clinical system validation, privacy, and security requirements may exceed a part-time founder's initial capacity
Incorrect payment instructions could damage site relationships
Large established site-payment vendors may move downmarket
Long sponsor procurement cycles could delay revenue

structure.commercial_archetype: Vertical payment-operations platform with implementation and per-accepted-event fees
structure.control_point: The jointly auditable mapping from protocol budget and site contract to accepted participant visit, data milestone, payment instruction, and remittance line
structure.critical_dependency: Sponsors must grant secure EDC or CTMS milestone access and authority to generate payment instructions under privacy and clinical-quality controls

thesis: Small EU biotech sponsors and CROs could use a lightweight payment-operations layer that maps negotiated site budgets to pseudonymous accepted visit and data-clean events, generates payment instructions through an existing provider, and returns detailed remittance receipts to both sponsor and site. The wedge is transparent event-to-payment reconciliation for smaller programmes, not a replacement for clinical or banking systems.
title: Trial Visit Paymaster Lite
uncertainties: Whether small sponsors experience enough reconciliation pain to buy a separate layer
Minimum integration scope acceptable to EDC and CTMS vendors
Whether sponsors will expose pseudonymous event status to a new provider
Actual implementation effort per unique site budget
